newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut shares end week mixed.
newsitem.headline: Beirut shares end week mixed.

text.p: Bank shares were mixed on sharply reduced turnover on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Friday and dealers said they expected Banque Audi to rise slowly in the next few weeks.
The BLOM stock index fell 0.57 percent to 903.33 while the LISPI share index rose 0.01 percent to 81.57.
Banque Audi, which has performed strongly since its January 20 debut, closed at $17 from last week's $17.25 after going ex-dividend.

It announced its first dividend on Monday at 40 cents, payable on March 3 to shareholders registered at February 24. Brokers said the fact that the price difference after the dividend was less than 40 cents indicated that the shares were actually up on the day.
They held at $17 for the rest of the week.
"The share will be more or less steady in the coming few weeks with a slow upward trend," a dealer said.
Turnover in Banque Audi shares fell to 81,461 shares from 162,310.
"There has been a lot of demand but not enough supply as most shareholders are keen to keep their shares because of price appreciation," the dealer said.
The other listed bank, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce, rose slightly to $12.625 from $12.5 but turnover also fell sharply to 42,960 from 102,706.
"BLC will continue varying between $12 and $12.5," the dealer, who wished not to be identified, added.
Solidere A shares, distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district Solidere is rebuilding, dropped to $10.375 from $10.5.
B shares, issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994, also fell to $10.75 from $10.875.
"The problem is still the oversupply. The A shares are being partially sold on the limit down," the dealer said.
Total offer during the week of A shares, which are still being distributed by Solidere, was 13 million while demand was only 219,576.

Also traded were 3,100 Ciments Libanais shares at $1.1875 slightly up from $1.1562 on February 14 when they were last traded. Some 3,000 Eternit shares were traded at $1.625, the price at which they last traded on July 2.
Market turnover fell to 407,075 from 527,247 during the week and value fell to $4,832,337 from $6,602,540.
There was no trade in the two other listed firms: Uniceramic and Ciments Blancs.
